title: Only 6% Of Adults Can Pass This Police Officer Entrance Exam
summary: Ten questions test judgment, communication, evidence handling and professional integrity.

landing.intro: The first calls seem straightforward. Then the exam moves into evidence, judgment and split-second decisions.

about.body:
This ten-question entertainment challenge uses broad principles that are relevant to professional policing across Tier 1 English-speaking countries. It tests safety-first judgment, careful witness communication, evidence integrity and accountable decision-making without relying on one country’s laws, ranks or procedures.

Choose one answer for each situation. Correctness stays hidden until the final reveal, where the complete answer review is available to unlock.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Answer ten increasingly difficult police aptitude questions.
Choose the safest, clearest or best-supported response.
Reveal your score, then unlock every answer you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an official police recruitment, legal, fitness, medical, psychological or employment assessment. Laws and operational procedures vary by jurisdiction.

stage-1.preAdCopy: Your ten answers have been checked and your police aptitude score is ready to reveal.

profile-1.title: The Exceptional Candidate
profile-1.copy: You combined calm judgment, precise communication and strong evidence awareness across the entire exam. Even the final integrity decisions stayed clear.

profile-2.title: The Entrance Exam Standout
profile-2.copy: You passed a challenge that catches out most adults. Your strongest answers balanced safety, fairness and factual thinking under pressure.

profile-3.title: The Calm Problem Solver
profile-3.copy: You showed dependable instincts across a difficult mix of situations. A few fine details in evidence or communication kept the pass mark just out of reach.

profile-4.title: The Promising Recruit
profile-4.copy: Your foundations are taking shape, while the more exact procedural and ethical questions proved tougher. The answer review connects every missed clue.

profile-5.title: The First-Day Cadet
profile-5.copy: This exam moved quickly from familiar situations into demanding professional judgment. Your strongest category shows where your instincts already stand out.

police-q1.question: You arrive at a scene where someone faces an immediate threat. What is the first priority?
answers: Protect life and make the scene as safe as possible
Begin a detailed written report
Collect every witness statement
Work out who is legally responsible

police-q2.question: Which opening question is most likely to produce a witness’s own uninterrupted account?
answers: The person in red started it, correct?
Please tell me what happened from the beginning
You did not see the whole incident, did you?
Was the suspect angry or frightened?

police-q3.question: Why may witnesses be kept apart before their initial accounts are taken?
answers: To make the interviews shorter
To decide who is most confident
To reduce the chance that their memories influence one another
To guarantee that every account matches

police-q4.question: What is the main purpose of a documented chain of custody?
answers: To rank evidence by importance
To prove a suspect owned every item
To replace photographs of the scene
To record who handled evidence and preserve its integrity

police-q5.question: Which set of principles best describes responsible use of police powers?
answers: Lawful, necessary, proportionate and accountable
Fast, secret, forceful and final
Popular, convenient, informal and broad
Automatic, identical, unlimited and unquestioned

police-q6.question: In the international spelling alphabet, which word represents the letter B?
answers: Baker
Bravo
Beta
Boston

police-q7.question: Which approach is most consistent with de-escalating a tense but non-immediate situation?
answers: Speak rapidly and move closer without warning
Issue several competing instructions at once
Use calm, clear language, listen and allow safe space
Raise your voice before anyone else can speak

police-q8.question: When safe and practical, what should happen before an important item at a scene is moved?
answers: It should be cleaned
It should be shown to every witness
It should be placed with similar items
Its original position and condition should be documented

police-q9.question: You discover a factual error in a report you submitted. What is the most professional response?
answers: Report and correct it promptly through the proper process
Wait to see whether anyone notices
Delete the entire report without a record
Ask a colleague to take responsibility

police-q10.question: Which radio message is most useful during a fast-moving incident?
answers: A long personal theory with no location
A concise factual update with the exact location and help required
Several unconfirmed rumours delivered at once
A vague request to send someone somewhere
